provenance:
PR (M40) round 2 cold review, task T-M40-1. `/smoke/stream` launches a real Chromium — the same resource a run launches, on a PaaS container sized for exactly one — and on this base it took nothing at all: no `SEM`, no check. Two tabs on the Browser check button launched two Chromiums, a `POST /tasks` inside a check's ~15s window launched the second, and `/readyz` answered `{ready: true, busy: false, active_run_id: null}` the whole time, because it reads `SEM` and the smoke path never touched it. The second Chromium is the OOM the single run slot exists to prevent, and it lands on the agent's record. Watched red against the unguarded base with all five: `first_stream_never_launched` absent (it did launch), `second_stream_launched_a_second_browser: [start, launching, error]`, `second_stream_not_refused`, `slot_not_held_while_smoke_runs: false`, `readyz_ready_while_a_browser_is_up: {ready: true, busy: false, ...}`, `slot_not_held_at_launching: [start, launching]`.

Graded through the real endpoint on the server's own loop, because the reported repro is two concurrent `curl -N`. No Chromium is launched and no timing margin is derived, because there is no race to leave margin for: playwright's entry point is swapped for a stub that parks at `launch()` on a `threading.Event` this case sets once the concurrent assertions are made, so the held window is exactly as long as the checks take (~20ms) instead of a `hold_seconds` sleep like `readyz-tracks-the-run-slot` needs. The stub caps its own park at 10s so a wiring mistake fails loudly rather than hanging the suite (CLAUDE.md rule 4).

The first assertion is the adversarial one: a guard that refuses EVERY browser check satisfies every other line here, so the case requires stream one to reach `launching` and only stream two to be refused. The last two are the leak: a semaphore taken and not returned bricks the service permanently, which is strictly worse than the bug being fixed. The error path is covered through HTTP (the stub raises where the real launch would, and `/readyz` must be idle after), and the client-went-away path in-process — `smoke_events()` driven to `launching`, then `aclose()`, which is the `GeneratorExit` a closed tab produces once Starlette cancels the stream task.

triage.note: The fix is a non-blocking try-acquire, not `async with SEM`: a browser check that queues behind a 60s run and then opens Chromium after the visitor has gone is a worse outcome than one that says busy immediately. `error` is the refusal event rather than a new `busy` event because the frontend's EventSource handler closes the stream on `done`/`error` only — a new event name would leave the spinner running forever, and the refusal text is what the panel shows. The console branch is graded as a substring of `PAGE` rather than by rendering it: `ui-rendered` is the machinery for the latter and it costs a browser launch.
triage.not_covered: The success path's release is not graded — the stub raises where the real launch is, so only the exception path and the generator-close path run their `finally` here. Both share one `finally` with the success path, so the untested arm is the same three lines. Nothing here launches a real browser or proves the container survives one; `agent-launches-its-own-browser` is the case that opens Chromium.
